name: MathVista
description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (i.e., IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). Completing these tasks requires fine-grained, deep visual understanding and compositional reasoning.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research)
citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024.
rai:dataCollection: MathVista incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets, including 9 math-targeted question answering (MathQA) datasets and 19 VQA datasets. Each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure a balanced representation. In total, 2,666 examples were collected from MathQA datasets and 2,739 from VQA datasets. Additionally, three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were created to address missing types of mathematical reasoning over specific visual contexts. IQTest comprises 228 examples sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms. FunctionQA contains 400 examples emphasizing algebraic reasoning concerning functional plots. PaperQA includes 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface, featuring questions derived from informative academic illustrations.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Web API
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data was collected from 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) and 3 newly created datasets. MathQA datasets include sources for geometry problem solving (GPS), math word problems (MWP) with visual contexts, and textbook question answering (TQA) on college curricula. VQA datasets were reviewed from over 70 candidates, selecting 19 that contain math-related instances and are publicly available. For the newly created datasets: IQTest was sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms, FunctionQA emphasized functional plots, and PaperQA was sourced from academic papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates. Examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Three expert annotators then manually labeled these examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning using majority voting. Each source dataset was limited to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. Quality checks were conducted to address unidentified errors.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For the three newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA), all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and further refined through a rigorous review process. A two-step process was employed: initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, resulting in a high inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%. Among the newly collected 736 questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements in the annotated answers. These discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team, ensuring consensus was reached on each example. For VQA dataset filtering, three expert annotators manually labeled examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using majority voting. The Fleiss Kappa score for inter-annotator agreement was 0.775, indicating substantial consistency.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tool (GUI shown in Figure 23 for new datasets, Figure 22 for VQA filtering, and Figure 24 for mathematical reasoning labeling)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For the newly created datasets, inter-annotation consistency was 99.2% among three reviewers, with only 6 disagreements out of 736 questions. For VQA dataset filtering, the Fleiss Kappa score was 0.775, indicating substantial inter-annotator agreement. For automatic annotation of mathematical reasoning categories, 94.1% of examples from automatic and human annotations had the exact same set of reasoning types, while 98.79% of individual labels were identical, indicating high accuracy of automatic annotation.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields for new dataset annotation. Expert annotators for VQA filtering and mathematical reasoning labeling.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: EasyOCR for OCR text detection, Multimodal Bard for image caption generation
rai:dataBiases: The authors acknowledge that questions in MathVista may be biased toward certain educational standards and curricula. The dataset contains 6.57% non-English questions (including Chinese and Persian), which may limit cross-lingual generalization. The dataset focuses on specific domains like science and college-level math, which may not represent all mathematical reasoning scenarios. Some visual contexts and mathematical reasoning types are underrepresented compared to others.
rai:dataLimitations: While MathVista encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts, spanning specific domains like science and college-level math, necessitates a more labor-intensive process for collecting high-quality data compared to textual-only or general-purpose datasets. Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure. The scalability and generalizability of the benchmark to other domains remain a concern.
rai:dataUseCases: MathVista is designed for evaluating mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts. It can be used for: (1) Training and testing large language models (LLMs) and large multimodal models (LMMs) on mathematical reasoning tasks, (2) Benchmarking model performance across different mathematical reasoning types (algebraic, arithmetic, geometry, logical, numeric commonsense, scientific, statistical), (3) Assessing model capabilities across diverse visual contexts (natural images, geometry diagrams, charts, plots, tables, etc.), (4) Model development validation using the testmini subset (1,000 examples), (5) Standard evaluation using the test subset (5,141 examples). The dataset is intended for research purposes to advance the development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks.
